recipes.name: Chef John's Salmon
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) center-cut salmon fillets, with skin

steps.text: Season salmon fillets with kosher salt. Line a baking sheet with foil and brush lightly with vegetable oil.
Preheat the oven's broiler to high and set the oven rack about 8 inches from heat source.
Process garlic, tarragon, and parsley in a blender or in a mortar and pestle to form a loose paste.
Mix mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, and cayenne pepper into garlic-herb mixture until combined.
Place salmon fillets, skin-side-down, on the baking sheet. Spread herb mixture over the top and sides of each fillet.
Cook under the preheated broiler until fillets are well-browned, about 5 minutes. Turn the broiler off and turn the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake until internal temperature of salmon is 130 degrees F (55 degrees C) and salmon flakes easily with a fork, about 3 to 4 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Salmon
raw_recipe.description: These broiled salmon fillets are coated with a herb mayonnaise flavored with garlic, lemon, and Dijon mustard to make an easy, elegant fish dinner.

video.description: Watch Chef John broil a simply delicious herb-crusted salmon.

review.reviewBody: This salmon is delicious! I used a wild salmon filet and was worried that the topping would overwhelm the natural salmon goodness, but it only added to it. I minced the garlic and mixed with the other ingredients (no food processesor necessary, imo). I subbed fresh thyme for tarragon, as I did not have any fresh tarragon. I think fresh dill would be great, too. I ended up baking at 400 for abut ten minutes, according to a similar recipe, and it worked out fine, although, I will broil next time for the added browning effect of the topping. I would definitely try this technique with other fish, too.
Delicious and easy to make. I'd use 2 tbs of mayo instead of 3. Also, sprinkle the lime juice on the filets first to soak in, then add the paste as per.

I only tried the cooking technique here, not the full recipe. I get the Salmon Milano from Costco (salmon with an herb butter) and used the broil then bake technique. It was the best-cooked salmon I've ever had! I usually use broil after baking, so this intrigued me, and it did not disappoint! (None of Chef John's recipes have EVER disappointed!!!)

I loved the simplicity of this perfectly flavored recipe. I was thrilled! I used dried parsley and fresh thyme (what I had on hand). Used dried mustard too because I didn't have fresh. I also baked the salmon for about 9 minutes (my fillets were huge) and it wasn't overcooked. A meat thermometer is a must, in my opinion. Served with green beens and a rice medley. I actually look for "Chef John's" recipes because they are usually so easy to make and I love the notes on how to tweak, if needed. Will definitely be making again, and again.

This is an amazing recipe I've made several times. I follow the recipe except I don't have fresh herbs. I use a French herb blend that includes tarragon and parsley. I don't blend, just mix it all together. My broiler isn't working so I baked a large salmon filet at 450 for about 25 min. I started checking it at 15 min. My granddaughter wanted seconds! I served the fish with basmati rice and asparagus. Thank You Chef John!
Made with dried dill, parsley, cayenne, lemon juice, dijon and greek yogurt. My oldest gobbled it up! I broiled for about 12 minutes; no baking. Next time I will try with tarragon and avocado mayo.
For a quick work night dinner, I used Costco pesto plus the Mayo and mustard. And broiled only as we like our wild salmon rare. Winner! I make it often.

Great new way of fixing salmon for us. Hubby and I both loved this dish! Only thing I did different was used dried herbs (not venturing out for fresh during Covid19), and added a little Planko & Parmesan to the top. Delicious!

This was great! I cooked it from frozen so I did 15 minutes covered under foil and the rest open. Fresh tarragon and fresh parsley really made the difference. It could probably do with a little less mayonnaise, but 3 tbsp. made a generous amount to spread on veggies a bit too. I made Chef John’s kale salad to go with it and it went very well together.

My family and I love this salmon and make it quite often!! It’s the one meal my daughter always requests when she’s home from college. I do make a couple of changes though. I use non-fat Greek yogurt instead of the mayonnaise and dill weed instead of the tarragon. For some reason my broiled salmon never really gets that brown 🙁 but it doesn’t take away from the taste. Easy and delicious recipe!

This was the best salmon we have had. We are in Florida for the month, so I started with salmon that had not been frozen, which makes a difference. I substituted dill for tarragon, and it was delicious. Our filet was thick and require nearly an extra 5 minutes in the oven after broiling.
Made as is and came out perfect. Got many compliments!
This is wonderful! I used dill instead of tarragon only because I did not have it. This is some of the best salmon I have ever made.
As is, perfect!

This was a sophisticated (but easy) recipe in which to use my home grown tarragon! The whole family loved this rendition for salmon. I tend not to use my broiler for too much cooking, but I did place the topped salmon pieces under the broiler for 5 minutes, which yielded a fairly light brown color, not the dark color as shown in the magazine or website photo. I was satisfied with this amount of color and turned the oven on to 400. I placed the steaks in immediately and they baked for about 15 minutes--perfectly done.
Really delicious! I used dried tarragon and dill instead of fresh tarragon and parsley. Everything else was per the recipe. I paired it with cilantro lime brown rice and asparagus spears.
This is a great recipe! Truly delicious and easy to make. I followed the recipe as written and will certainly make it again.

Tonight, the only fresh herbs I had were dill and cilantro, plus garlic, of course. I never would have thought to combine cilantro and dill, but OMGosh. It was delicious! We'll definitely make it again, and I'll experiment with different herbs in the future. (Btw, I used olive oil mayo.) Thanks once again, Chef John.
Good, my husband really liked it. I had to use dried tarragon and parsley, homemade Dijon. I'll try again with fresh spices, real Dijon.
OMG!!!!! So tasty and versatile
